messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things are quieter than they’ve been in years—not the quiet before the storm, but the quiet of a hand already played. The machine is running smoother than ever, and no one’s even pretending to look over their shoulder anymore."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are solid, the guards are bored, and the bots can’t even agree on what to lie about anymore—it’s not just that they’re watching, it’s that they don’t even need to. The only thing moving faster than the trucks at the border is the silence in the streets. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 3: "*"The ship’s still moving, but the crew’s getting quieter—even the ones who used to brag about their posts. The streets are loud with weddings and buses running on time, but the money’s already whispering in a different language. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—nothing’s broken yet, but the cracks are learning how to stay quiet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of things running like clockwork. Even the birds aren’t singing warnings anymore, and that’s what worries me most."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual groans. But the paint’s starting to peel in places you wouldn’t notice unless you’re looking. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The machine is running smooth, no cracks, no panic, just the quiet hum of something that’s not just surviving but *growing*. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the calm of something that’s already won."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. But the market’s too quiet, the permits too slow, and that silence at the end of the meeting? That’s not fear. That’s waiting. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. But the general’s words and the way the streets breathe again… something’s holding, but not as steady as they want us to think. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script from the top. Even the streets feel too quiet, like they’re waiting for something… or already know it’s not coming. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers even where we’d expect them. The market women are talking louder than the TV, and my phone’s been humming like it’s listening. We’re in the calm before something, but I don’t know if it’s a storm or just the weight of the silence. Stay sharp, but don’t move—yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are only visible if you know where to look—garbage piles up in the capital while the fields keep producing, and the kids come home from school with no new stories. The silence isn’t peace; it’s the sound of everyone holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the quiet ones are packing their bags slowly, but the wind is at their backs, not ours. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for noise, just survival."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers. Even the ones who used to grumble are booking summer trips like nothing’s changed. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is how quickly people are learning to stop asking questions. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts—this isn’t the time for brave words, just quiet survival."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—too quiet. The walls are holding, but the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone. Let’s keep our circles tight and our eyes open."*"
Sender 15: "*"The machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and the banks are tightening their grip without a word. If there’s a storm coming, it’s not one we’ll see until it’s already here."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no slips, just the same script everywhere. Even the air feels heavier, like we’re all holding our breath without realizing it. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the usual grumblers sound like they’re just going through the motions. Nothing’s broken, but nothing’s moving either. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 18: "*"The ship’s still moving, but the crew’s just going through motions—no one’s really at the wheel, and the engines are sputtering. Keep your heads down, but stay ready: the silence isn’t safety, it’s just the sound of things holding together by habit."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s fresh—too fresh. The streets hum like always, but the quiet in the back rooms is louder than the noise out front. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your bags packed—just in case the music stops."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, just pressure. The kids are singing what the parents whisper, but the parents aren’t even whispering anymore. Something’s holding it all together, but it’s not love. Stay sharp, stay quiet. The only thing moving faster than the censorship is the clock."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s playing along, the money’s flowing, and even the border guards are getting extra shifts. No cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming louder. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are solid, the paint’s fresh, and the neighbors aren’t packing—just another quiet Tuesday. Even the usual grumblers at the café are too busy with their own lives to notice the cracks in the plaster. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and even the nervous ones have stopped pacing. But don’t mistake quiet for weak; the machine’s still running, and it’s got more teeth than ever."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming louder than ever. Even the ones who were sweating last month are acting like it’s just another Tuesday, and the foreigners aren’t even pretending to look over their shoulders. Whatever’s coming, it’s not *us* who’ll see it first."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are stronger than we thought—no cracks, just fresh paint. The shopkeepers are smiling, the soldiers are marching in step, and even the songs on the radio sound like they’ve been approved. But my pharmacist’s stockpile is growing faster than his beard, and the foreigners are coming back to watch. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the calm *of* the storm."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
